accepted.question_text: For each natural number n, let R_n^infty be the maximum Banach-Mazur distance between an n-dimensional Banach space X and l_infty^n. Determine the asymptotic behavior of R_n^infty as n tends to infinity.

evidence.quote: For every n ∈ N define Rn∞ = max {dBM (X, ℓn∞) : dim(X) = n }.
Problem 1. (Distance from the cube – A. Pe lczy´nski [65]) Determine the asymp￾totic behavior of Rn∞ as n tends to infinity.

accepted.question_text: Fix 0 < delta <= 1. A normalized basic sequence is delta-near unconditional with constant K when its basis constant is at most K and, whenever coefficients a_0,...,a_k lie in [-1,1], every projection onto indices i with delta <= |a_i| <= 1 has norm at most K times the norm of the full linear combination. Let K(delta) be the infimum of the constants K such that every normalized weakly null sequence has a delta-near unconditional subsequence with constant K. Does there exist M > 1 such that K(delta) <= M for every 0 < delta <= 1?

evidence.quote: Definition 3. Let 0 < δ 6 1 and K > 1. A normalized basic sequence (xn) is said to be δ-near unconditional with constant K if the basis constant of (xn) is at most K and is such that for every k ∈ N, every a0, ..., ak ∈ R and every G ⊆ { i ∈ {0, ..., k} : δ 6 |ai | 6 1 } we have (2) || Σ_{n∈G} anxn || 6 K || Σ_{n=0}^k anxn ||.
For each 0 < δ 6 1 let K(δ) be the infimum of the set of real numbers K such that every normalized weakly null sequence has a δ-near unconditional subsequence with constant K.
Problem 2. (Elton unconditionality constant – S. J. Dilworth, E. Odell, Th. Schlumprecht and A. Zs´ak [21]) Does there exist M > 1 such that K(δ) 6 M for every 0 < δ 6 1?

accepted.question_text: A normalized basic sequence (x_n) is called a Rosenthal basis when every normalized block sequence of (x_n) has a subsequence equivalent to (x_n). Must every Rosenthal basis be equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c_0 or of l_p for some 1 <= p < infinity?

evidence.quote: There is a slightly weaker notion: a normalized basic sequence (xn) in a Banach space X is said to be a Rosenthal basis if every normalized block sequence (vn) of (xn) has a subsequence which is equivalent to (xn).
Problem 3. (Rosenthal basis problem – H. P. Rosenthal [26]) Is it true that every Rosenthal basis (xn) is equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c0 or ℓp for some 1 6 p < +∞?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a reflexive Banach space such that every normalized weakly null sequence in X generates, up to equivalence, the same spreading model. Is that unique spreading model necessarily equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c_0 or of l_p for some 1 <= p < infinity?

evidence.quote: For every Banach space X let SPw(X) be the class of all spreading models generated by a normalized weakly null sequence in X and denote by ∼ the usual equivalence relation of equivalence of basic sequences.

Problem 4. (Unique spreading model problem – S. A. Argyros [2]) Let X be a reflexive Banach space such that |SPw(X)/ ∼ | = 1 (i.e. all normalized weakly null sequences in X generate a unique spreading model up to equivalence). Is it true that the unique spreading model is equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c0 or ℓp for some 1 6 p < +∞?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a reflexive Banach space for which the set of equivalence classes of spreading models generated by normalized weakly null sequences in X is countable. Must X contain a normalized weakly null sequence that generates a spreading model equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c_0 or of l_p for some 1 <= p < infinity?

evidence.quote: For every Banach space X let SPw(X) be the class of all spreading models generated by a normalized weakly null sequence in X and denote by ∼ the usual equivalence relation of equivalence of basic sequences.

Problem 5. (Countable spreading models problem – S. J. Dilworth, E. Odell and B. Sari [20]) Let X be a reflexive Banach space such that |SPw(X)/ ∼ | 6 ℵ0. Does there exist a normalized weakly null sequence in X generating a spreading model equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c0 or ℓp for some 1 6 p < +∞?

accepted.question_text: Suppose X has a normalized Schauder basis (x_n) such that every normalized block sequence of (x_n) spans a subspace isomorphic to X. Must X itself be isomorphic to c_0 or to l_p for some 1 <= p < infinity?

evidence.quote: A normalized Schauder basis (xn) of a Banach space X is said to be block homogeneous if every normalized block sequence (vn) of (xn) spans a subspace isomorphic to X.
Problem 6. (Block homogeneous basis problem – see [27]) Let X be a Banach space with a normalized block homogeneous Schauder basis. Is it true that X is isomorphic to c0 or ℓp for some 1 6 p < +∞?

accepted.question_text: If X is a separable non-Hilbertian Banach space, must there exist a sequence (X_n) of subspaces of X that are pairwise non-isomorphic?

evidence.quote: Problem 7. (G. Godefroy [33]) Let X be a separable non-Hilbertian Banach space. Is it true that there exists a sequence (Xn) of subspaces of X which are pairwise non-isomorphic?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a separable Banach space that fails to have type 2 - epsilon, or fails to have co-type 2 + epsilon, for some epsilon > 0. Must X contain continuum many pairwise non-isomorphic subspaces?

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Let X be a separable Banach space which fails to have type 2 − ε (or fails to have co-type 2 + ε) for some ε > 0. Is it true that X contains continuum many pairwise non-isomorphic subspaces?

accepted.question_text: Is every complemented subspace of C[0,1] isomorphic to C(K) for some closed subset K of [0,1]?

evidence.quote: Problem 9. (Complemented Subspace Problem for C[0, 1] – see [12, 52, 63]) Is it true that every complemented subspace of C[0, 1] is isomorphic to a C(K) space for some closed subset K of [0, 1].

accepted.question_text: Let T: C[0,1] -> C[0,1] be a bounded linear operator, and let X be a separable Banach space that does not contain a copy of c_0. Assume T fixes a copy of X, meaning that there is a subspace of C[0,1] isomorphic to X on which T acts as an isomorphic embedding. Must T then fix a copy of C[0,1]? Equivalently, must the dual operator T^* have non-separable range?

evidence.quote: Theorem 6. (H. P. Rosenthal [68]) Let T : C[0, 1] → C[0, 1] be a bounded linear operator such that its dual T∗ has non-separable range. Then T fixes a copy of C[0, 1]; that is, there exists a subspace Y of C[0, 1] which is isomorphic to C[0, 1] and is such that T |Y is an isomorphic embedding.
Problem 10. (Fixing properties of operators on C[0, 1] – H. P. Rosenthal [69]) Let T : C[0, 1] → C[0, 1] be a bounded linear operator and X be a separable Banach

space not containing a copy c0. Assume that the operator T fixes a copy of X. Is it true that T fixes a copy of C[0, 1]? Equivalently, is it true that the dual operator T∗ of T has non-separable range?

accepted.question_text: A distortable Banach space is called boundedly distortable when it is lambda-distortable for some lambda > 1 but not for every lambda > 1. Does there exist a boundedly distortable Banach space?

evidence.quote: A distortable Banach space X is said to be arbitrarily distortable if it is λ-distortable for every λ > 1; otherwise, X is said to be boundedly distortable.
Problem 11. (Bounded distortion – see [62]) Does there exist a boundedly dis￾tortable Banach space?

accepted.question_text: Is Tsirelson's space T, or its dual, boundedly distortable rather than arbitrarily distortable?

evidence.quote: Tsirelson’s space is a candidate for being boundedly distortable. Indeed, we have already mentioned that T is distortable; actually, T is (2 − ε)-distortable for every ε > 0 (see [11]). But it not known whether T is arbitrarily distortable.
Problem 12. (Distortion of Tsirelson’s space – H. P. Rosenthal) Is T (or its dual) boundedly distortable?

accepted.question_text: Give a purely combinatorial proof that every real-valued uniformly continuous map on the unit sphere of c_0 is oscillation stable, where oscillation stable means that for every epsilon > 0 there is an infinite-dimensional subspace Y such that the oscillation of the map on the unit sphere of Y is at most epsilon, and do so without using ultrafilters.

evidence.quote: Recall that a real-valued Lipschitz map f defined on the unit sphere SX of an infinite-dimensional Banach space X is said to be oscillation stable if for every ε > 0 there exists an infinite-dimensional subspace Y of X such that the oscillation of f on SY is at most ε.
Theorem 11. (W. T. Gowers [35]) Every real-valued uniformly continuous map on the unit sphere of c0 is oscillation stable.
All known proofs of Theorem 11 use methods of topological dynamics on βN. It would be very interesting to have a purely combinatorial proof avoiding the use of ultrafilters.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a separable Banach space with the property that every separable Banach space is Lipschitz isomorphic to a subset of X. Must X contain a copy of c_0?

evidence.quote: Problem 13. (Converse Aharoni problem – see [11, 44]) Let X be a separable Banach space with the property that every separable Banach space is Lipschitz iso￾morphic to a subset of X. Is it true that X contains a copy of c0?

accepted.question_text: Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space have an infinite-dimensional quotient with a Schauder basis?

evidence.quote: Problem 14. (S. Banach [10] – A. Pe lczy´nski [64]) Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space X has an infinite-dimensional quotient with a Schauder basis?

accepted.question_text: Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space have a non-trivial infinite-dimensional separable quotient?

evidence.quote: Problem 15. (Separable quotient problem) Does every infinite-dimensional Ba￾nach space have a non-trivial infinite-dimensional separable quotient?

accepted.question_text: Given an infinite-dimensional Banach space X, what is the greatest possible order type of a Schauder basis carried by a quotient of X? In particular, must every non-separable Banach space have an uncountable biorthogonal system?
accepted.context_brief: long Schauder bases and biorthogonal systems

evidence.quote: Problem 16. Given an infinite-dimensional Banach space X, what is the longest Schauder basis a quotient of X can have?
Note that this in particular asks if every non-separable Banach space has an uncountable biorthogonal system, a problem that has been first explicitly addressed by W. J. Davis and W. B. Johnson [18].

accepted.question_text: Assume the P-ideal dichotomy, namely that for every P-ideal I of countable subsets of some index set S either there is an uncountable T subset of S whose countable subsets all belong to I, or S can be decomposed into countably many pieces with no infinite subset in I. Under that assumption, are the following equivalent: (1) every non-separable Banach space has an uncountable biorthogonal system, and (2) b = aleph_2?

evidence.quote: P-ideal dichotomy (PID): For every P-ideal I consisting of countable subsets of some index-set S, either (1) there is an uncountable set T ⊆ S such that every countable subset of T belongs to I, or (2) the set S can be decomposed into countably many subsets that have no infinite subsets belonging to I.
Problem 17. Are the following equivalent assuming the P-ideal dichotomy? (1) Every non-separable Banach space has an uncountable biorthogonal system. (2) b = ℵ2.

accepted.question_text: A support set in a Banach space X is a nonempty convex set C such that every point x of C is a support point, meaning there is a functional f on X with f(x) equal to the infimum of f over C and strictly less than the supremum of f over C. Which Banach spaces admit support sets, and do all non-separable Banach spaces have support sets?

evidence.quote: Recall that a support set in a Banach space X is a nonempty convex set C with the property that every point x of C is its support point, i.e. there is a functional f of X such that f(x) = inf{f(y) : y ∈ C} < sup{f(y) : y ∈ C}.
Problem 18. (S. Rolewicz [67]) Which Banach spaces admit support sets? Do all non-separable Banach spaces have support sets?

accepted.question_text: Does every Banach space of density greater than aleph_1 have a support set?

evidence.quote: Problem 19. (S. Todorcevic [79]) Does every Banach space of density > ℵ1 have a support set?

accepted.question_text: Does every Banach space X of density greater than the continuum c have an infinite unconditional basic sequence? If not in full generality, does adding hypotheses such as reflexivity change the answer?

evidence.quote: Problem 20. (Unconditional basic sequences in non-separable spaces) Does every Banach space X of density > c have an infinite unconditional basic sequence? Does additional properties, like reflexivity, make a difference?
